meta.evidence_status: SIMULATION-DERIVED ANALYSIS: synthetic handwriting and tremor through the coupled pen simulator (model M1); not a measurement of any person or device
meta.reference: deposited-ink position 'tip' of each simulator trace at 1 kHz (float32, decimated by sim/run_nominal.py from the 2 kHz simulation; scenario per results/sim/nominal/metrics.json: test seed 200, 9 Hz 0.3 mm tremor, altitude 50 deg, 1 N); strokes = contiguous 'contact' runs; page origin = first contact position

variants.format_point: ICD 0x02 as specified: instantaneous sample every 5 ms, x/y rounded to 1 um (headline)
variants.sampling_only: 200 Hz point sampling without rounding (isolates temporal sampling)
variants.quantisation_only: 1 kHz reference rounded to 1 um (isolates spatial quantisation)
variants.format_boxcar5: 200 Hz from a centred 5-sample (5 ms) boxcar mean, rounded to 1 um (alternative decimation)
variants.format_point_endpoints: format_point plus extra samples at the pen-down and pen-up instants (proposed ICD change)

method.phase_note: the 5 ms sampling grid is evaluated at every 1 ms offset; worst cases are over phases
method.time_aligned_deviation: captured samples are linearly interpolated at the reference time stamps; reference points before the first / after the last captured sample are compared with that endpoint (end truncation). max/rms over all points; this coupling bounds the Frechet distance from above
method.frechet: exact discrete Frechet distance (Eiter-Mannila) between the reference and captured polylines after densifying both to edges <= 2.0 um; the continuous Frechet distance lies in [value - 2.0, value]
method.frechet_vertices_only: discrete Frechet on the raw vertex sets (1 kHz vs 200 Hz) is reported for the headline variant only to show its sampling bias: with sparse vertices it is dominated by half the inter-sample spacing, not by capture error
method.interp_bound: a_max * T^2 / 8 + sqrt(2)/2 um (linear interpolation + rounding), a_max from 1 kHz second differences

interpretation: Headline (format_point, main strokes, worst over traces and sampling phases): time-aligned max deviation 120.608 um, RMS 3.594 um; interior-only max 75.602 um, RMS 2.942 um; densified discrete Frechet max 120.608 um (median 46.771 um).
End truncation dominates the maximum: up to 120.608 um because the first/last sample can fall up to 4 ms inside the contact interval while the pen moves.
Adding samples at the pen-down/up instants reduces the max deviation to 81.52 um (end truncation 0.0 um).
1 um rounding alone contributes at most 0.704 um (RMS 0.409 um); the format error is sampling-dominated.
Short contacts (< 50 ms, bounces in the simulator): 22 of 60 phase-evaluations produced no sample and 38 a single sample; the format cannot represent them faithfully.

Scale for comparison (research ledger OPT-02): DeltaPen optical-flow tracking reports 0.068 mm mean absolute error per 10 ms window, i.e. the sensing error, not the stroke format, is expected to dominate capture error.
These figures describe the format applied to simulated ink; they say nothing about sensor accuracy, which must be measured (bench protocol).
